Ahead of the Punjab Assembly elections, three AAP MLAs joined BJP, in New Delhi on November 2, 2026. Photo: X/@BJP4India
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Monday (November 2, 2026) suffered a setback ahead of the Punjab Assembly election, due in early 2027, after three of its leaders — Kunwar Vijay Pratap, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jauramajra — joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in New Delhi.
Sanour MLA Mr. Pathanmajra and Samana MLA Mr. Jauramajra resigned from the party’s primary membership on Sunday (November 1, 2026). They both said they were quitting the AAP as it had failed to fulfil the promises it had made ahead of the 2022 Assembly election.
Amritsar North MLA Mr. Pratap, a former Indian Police Service officer, resigned as a legislator on Monday (November 2, 2026) morning to join the BJP later in the day. “There is an atmosphere of chaos all around Punjab. Drug abuse has reached alarming levels and a drug empire has been established. Extortion has now become an industry, and gangsterism is also at its peak,” Mr. Pratap said after joining the BJP.
AAP MLAs from Punjab, Shri Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, Shri Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Shri Chetan Singh Jauramajra #JoinBJP at the party headquarters in New Delhi. https://t.co/zmZLRDwLsO
Mr. Pratap has remained critical of the government’s handling of various sensitive issues, including the sluggish investigation into alleged incidents of the desecration of the Guru Granth Sahib and subsequent police firings at Behbal Kalan in Faridkot district that claimed the lives of two Sikh protesters in 2015.
He has also questioned the AAP’s touted ‘Schools of Eminence’. In 2023, ahead of AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal’s visit to inaugurate Punjab’s first School of Eminence in Amritsar, Mr. Pratap had pointed out that the school in question had only been “renovated”, and that it had been made a smart school by the previous governments.
In June 2025, Mr. Pratap was suspended from the party for five years for indulging in anti-party activities.
AAP leaders joining the BJP clearly indicated the impending end of the party’s regime in Punjab, the State BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon said, adding that the BJP’s “caravan in Punjab” was growing stronger by the day, with the ground reality turning decisively against the ruling party.
